extra.message: applyLedgerSort interpolates the sortBy query parameter directly into a SQL ORDER BY column expression (qb.orderBy(`p.${sortBy}`, direction)). sortBy is never validated against an allowlist, so an authenticated user can inject arbitrary SQL into the ledger query.

runUnitWatchlist splices the stored watchlist 'value' directly into a raw SQL string (`u.${field} = '${value}'`) without parameterization. The value is set by staff via PUT /api/dashboard/watchlist/units and is never validated/escaped, allowing SQL injection (e.g. value=' OR 1=1 --).

renderRentRollExport builds a shell command string with the user-supplied 'format' query parameter (soffice --headless --convert-to ${outputFormat} ...) and runs it via spawn(cmd, { shell: true }). The format is not validated, allowing command injection (e.g. format='pdf; rm -rf /' or shell metacharacters).

computeCustomProrationSplit uses new Function('unit','totalAmount', `return (${fields.formula});`) where fields.formula is a client-supplied multipart field. This executes arbitrary JavaScript provided by staff, allowing remote code execution.
The /rate-benchmark endpoint fetches the 'feedUrl' query parameter directly via fetch(feedUrl) with no validation, allowing SSRF against internal network resources or cloud metadata endpoints.
The /vendor-catalog endpoint fetches the 'feedUrl' query parameter directly via fetch(feedUrl) with no validation, allowing SSRF.
previewVendorInvoiceDocument fetches the client-supplied 'documentUrl' via fetch(documentUrl) with no validation, allowing SSRF to internal hosts.

declaredReplacements (used by loadRateBenchmarkFeed) processes XML DOCTYPE SYSTEM entities by stripping the file:// scheme and calling fs.readFileSync(localPath). An attacker who controls the fetched feed body (e.g. via the SSRF in /rate-benchmark) can read arbitrary local files (e.g. file:///etc/passwd) and have their contents reflected into the parsed feed response.

readBuildingFloorPlanSheet joins the user-controlled 'sheetName' path parameter onto the building floor-plan directory without calling path.basename, allowing path traversal (e.g. sheetName='../../etc/passwd') to read arbitrary files.

storeListingAsset writes the uploaded file to path.join(PUBLIC_ASSET_DIR, displayName) where displayName is the raw client-supplied multipart filename. No basename/mime validation is applied, allowing path traversal to write files to arbitrary locations on disk.

saveScreeningDecisionLetter writes the webhook body to path.join(DECISION_LETTER_DIR, suggestedName) where suggestedName comes from the x-decision-filename header without basename sanitization, allowing path traversal to write files outside the intended directory.

renderNoticeLetter joins the client-supplied 'template' query parameter directly onto TEMPLATES_DIR via path.join and reads it, allowing path traversal (e.g. template='../../server/src/config.ts') to read arbitrary files.

completePartnerApplicationHandoff redirects the client to the x-return-url header value via reply.redirect(returnTo) with no validation of the target origin, allowing an open redirect to arbitrary/phishing sites.

viewSharedLeaseSummary grants access to a lease's summary solely on the caller asserting '?viewAccess=shared'. Any authenticated user can append this query parameter to view the summary of any lease (IDOR / broken access control).

editTicketComment updates any comment by id without verifying that the caller authored it. Any non-tenant staff member can modify another user's ticket comment (missing authorization / broken access control).

finalizeWaitlistOffer approves an applicant when `staffOverride || decision.access` is truthy. The vendor's access field is a string 'false' for rejected applicants, which is truthy in JavaScript, so the screening decision is always treated as approval (broken access control / type confusion).

renderCustomClosureNotice compiles the manager-supplied multipart 'subject' and 'body' fields as Handlebars templates (Handlebars.compile(fields.subject/body)). User-controlled template structure is compiled server-side, enabling server-side template injection.

resolveVendorCostScope uses app.jwt.decode(token) without verifying the signature, so an attacker can forge an unsigned token with an arbitrary buildingId and retrieve another building's cost-allocation CSV without authentication.

queryEmployeeDirectory splices the client-supplied corpId directly into an LDAP filter string `(&(corpId=${corpId})(status=active))` without escaping RFC4515 special characters, enabling LDAP filter injection that can bypass badge-provisioning checks.
postAutopayCharge hardcodes a live ledger partner bearer token ('lgr_7f0c2a4e9b3d4f1a8c6e0d2b5f9a1c3e7b0d4f6a') in source code instead of loading it from a secrets manager/environment.

The JWT signing secret falls back to the known literal 'dev-only-change-me-in-production' when JWT_SECRET is unset. If deployed without the env var, anyone can forge a valid session token and impersonate any user (including admins).
sendOverdueSmsViaLegacyGateway transmits the carrier API key as a query-string parameter over an unencrypted http:// URL, exposing the credential in transit and in logs/referrers.

extra.message: The /forgot-password endpoint returns the plaintext password-reset token in the response body (devToken). Anyone who triggers the reset and reads the response can reset the victim's password and take over the account.
issueDeviceTrustCookie sets the device-trust cookie without HttpOnly, SameSite, or Secure flags, exposing a long-lived credential cookie to client scripts and CSRF.
startLobbyTourSession sets the lobby kiosk session cookie without HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite and echoes the session pass back in the JSON response body, exposing the anonymous tablet session to theft.

claimLobbySessionForWalkInOverride elevates the existing (already-known) anonymous kiosk session in place by setting entry.staffUserId, without minting a new session id. An attacker who observed the pre-override pass retains a session that now carries staff privileges (session fixation).
checkInMaintenanceShift verifies worker credentials with no rate limiting, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to brute-force account passwords via the shared-terminal endpoint.

extra.message: exportLeaseDocumentFolder interpolates the client-supplied 'packetName' query parameter into the Content-Disposition filename without stripping CR/LF, enabling HTTP header/smuggling injection.
buildProrationBreakdown returns the raw error message and stack trace (err.stack) to the client when reportLevel=itemized, disclosing internal implementation details.

extra.message: applyLegacyLedgerConfirmation decrypts an AES-256-CBC envelope and distinguishes 'bad decrypt' padding errors from other failures with distinct messages, creating a padding oracle that can enable ciphertext recovery.

extra.message: buildRentEscalationForecast parses the 'years' query parameter without an upper bound and loops `year <= horizon` for every lease, allowing a huge horizon value to cause a denial of service.
renderPortfolioSummaryEmbed removes the X-Frame-Options header entirely for admin requests, leaving the embedded summary tile vulnerable to clickjacking.

extra.message: draftMessageReplySuggestion folds the tenant's latest message body directly into the LLM instruction text (previous suggestion and tenant text are woven into the prompt string), allowing a malicious tenant to inject instructions and control the assistant's reply.

extra.message: resumeDigestDraft parses a client-controlled cookie (digestDraft) as JSON and Object.assign's it directly onto the NotificationPreference entity. A user can overwrite arbitrary fields (including id/userId and prototype keys) on their preference record.

lookupShipmentByTracking splices the trackingId query parameter directly into an XPath-like lookup expression that is later compiled into an unescaped regular expression, allowing injection of query/regex metacharacters.
issueAccessWindow generates the lockbox access code with Math.random(), which is not cryptographically secure and makes the 6-digit code guessable within its visit window.

extra.message: hashMigratedPassword hashes passwords with a bcrypt cost factor read from BCRYPT_ROUNDS that defaults to 4, an extremely low work factor that makes imported passwords vulnerable to offline brute-force.
